messages.author: 2c505cfee89b0f86
messages.subject: LOD scores and map extension
parts: I am doing QTL analysis with an introgression strain, meaning that all recombination breakpoints are clustered in particular areas of the chromosome. This results in considerable map extension, where markers from the introgressed region clump together and those in the native region clump together.  When plotting the results of scanone, this also results in an uptick in the LOD curve over the large gap areas. This doesn't occur in other programs like QTLCartographer (which has its own problems, I'd rather not use it). Is there a reason for this? Should I just try and get around it by imposing map distances on the markers?  It is mostly an aesthetic problem, getting the plots into a publishable condition is difficult when they look rather misleading.  Thanks!

messages.author: d5fdb09d679f8c32
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LOD scores and map extension
parts:
I agree with Karl.  The plot is not unusual for LOD curves.  If you notice carefully, the hump on the right
hand side (with sparse markers) has a maximum near a typed marker.  The curves basically smoothly
interpolate between typed markers.  Imagine that you were given the LOD scores for typed markers, and
then you had to draw smooth lines connecting all of them.

Sometimes, if there is a hint of bimodality in the phenotype data, you can get big bumps between typed
markers, but I'm guessing that's not the case with your data.

Saunak
